tutorSurveys: First session: introductions and getting to know each other.
Two of the four scholars were disruptive throughout the session (laughing, talking), not taking it seriously. Tutor spoke with them throughout to try to redirect.
Two scholars are struggling with multi-digit subtraction. I will continue to work with the scholars on subtraction.
Scholars were quiet, contributed when prompted.
All were engaged and participated in we do. Two scholars need more time with subtraction (Thais and Ameliah).

Ahlayna not paying attention. I spoke with her after class about needing to pay attention so she understands what is being taught. Told her that if she does not understand during the session to ask questions. This is a safe space to do that.
Second session of the week. I revised the teaching approach from the first session to deliver same information, and it was much better understood by scholars.
Scholars contributed and interacted, one only when prompted. More discussion in next session with recap and more I Do work.
Needed to align two scholars on classroom behavior to proceed with the lesson. Discussed putting an incentive plan in place with the next session.

Scholars had some difficulty in writing sentences with context clues as discussed and examples written on the board. Will tweak approach of teaching in the next group today to look for similar issues or better understanding. Will review with this group again in their next session to assess if they have a better grasp of the topic.

Scholars need more time to demonstrate how to use the four types of context clues when writing sentences. They were eager, but need a bit more practice. Will continue working on that in the next session.
That week, I had an issue with getting online (Wi-Fi) to take attendance and do surveys. On Monday, I will check the desk in the classroom for paper surveys.
Amelia needs help with basic addition of one digit numbers. Will give her sheets with simple one-digit math problems during the daily warm-up, and add one problem on the exit tickets
Students were hiding, did not want to come, heads down.
They were engaged, eager to read. Need to work with them on instructions like giving an example after the instructions.,
Delayed start as students were completing math instruction from first of two part class, and needing to reboot laptop to get back on wi-fi to access Pearl

New word meanings from a book for 3rd to 6th graders. The target words selected are new for most of the scholars. A lot is packed into the session time to help with understanding. In the second session, we will continue with discussion of the words as used in context of the reading.

Only two of four scholars in attendance. One was quiet, required prompting to speak. The other was outgoing and very much engaged. I will need to rethink how to deliver the second weekly session since two were out. Possibly redo session one with addition of one or two new vocabulary words to engage the scholars here today.
Nakory is not on my roster, she may be for NJESLA now? Need to confirm.
Could spend more time lecturing maybe . I feel like I had them writing constantly. The time went by so quick. 2 students were able to get to their exit ticket.

To early to say only a get to know session. However, this group seems receptive.
They did not seem interested at all. Not feeling that confident.

Having trouble with redirecting behavior. But front facing (me to the scholars) I believe they got the difference between reasoning and supporting details. How they differ and I want to build on this skill. Could do better with time management.
More getting to know the group, questions to learn their style of learning math, what they like, and what operations challenge them.
Just intros so not sure if this a good time to assess, but this group seemed receptive.
Introductions, collaborated on classroom rules, reviewed structure of the tutoring class steps (SEL, Warm-up, I Do, We Do...)
Getting to know scholars, what they like about math, what confuses them, and why.
